title: Advanced Inheritance: Commander Override
objectives: Learn method overriding in child classes
Understand how to use super() to call parent methods
Master polymorphism - same method, different behavior
Build complex hierarchies with multiple specialized classes
description: Final OOP lesson! Create Commander Droids with higher privileges by mastering method overriding and super(). Learn polymorphism - how different droid types can respond to the same command differently. Build a complete droid hierarchy for Neon City!

exercises.title: Method Overriding - Custom Greeting
exercises.instructions:
**Commander Privilege Protocol:**

Override the greet() method for Commanders to show authority!

**Task:**
1. Start with your Droid base class (with greet method)
2. Create a `CommanderDroid` child class
3. Override the `greet()` method to print:
   `"ATTENTION. Commander {self.name} taking control."`
4. Create a Commander: `leader = CommanderDroid('ALPHA-PRIME', 100)`
5. Call `leader.greet()`

**Key Concept:** The child's method REPLACES the parent's method!
hints: Just define a method with the same name to override it
The child's version is used instead of the parent's
Commanders need a more authoritative greeting!

exercises.title: Using super() - Extended Initialization
exercises.instructions:
**Rank Assignment System:**

Use super() to extend the __init__ method and add a rank attribute.

**Protocol:**
1. Create CommanderDroid class that inherits from Droid
2. Override `__init__` to accept name, battery_level, AND rank
3. Use `super().__init__(name, battery_level)` to call parent's init
4. Add `self.rank = rank` for the new attribute
5. Override `greet()` to print:
   `"Commander {self.name}, Rank {self.rank}, reporting."`
6. Create: `cmd = CommanderDroid('APEX-1', 100, 'General')`

**super() lets you avoid rewriting the parent code!**
exercises.expectedOutput:
Commander APEX-1, Rank General, reporting.
Battery: 100%
hints: super().__init__(name, battery_level) calls the parent's init
After super(), you can add new attributes like self.rank
This avoids copying self.name and self.battery_level code

exercises.title: Polymorphism - Factory Inspection
exercises.instructions:
**Final Factory Test - Polymorphism in Action:**

Create a mixed fleet and loop through them, calling greet() on each.

**Manufacturing Order:**
1. Use your complete Droid and CommanderDroid classes
2. Create a list called `fleet` with:
   - A Droid: `Droid('WORKER-1', 90)`
   - A Droid: `Droid('WORKER-2', 85)`
   - A CommanderDroid: `CommanderDroid('CHIEF-X', 100, 'Captain')`
3. Loop through the fleet: `for unit in fleet:`
4. Call `unit.greet()` on each

**Polymorphism:** Same method name, different behavior based on object type!

This is OOP mastery - Python knows which greet() to call!
exercises.expectedOutput:
=== FACTORY ROLL CALL ===
Greetings. I am WORKER-1, Worker Unit.
Greetings. I am WORKER-2, Worker Unit.
Commander CHIEF-X, Rank Captain, reporting.

✅ All units operational. Neon City Droid Factory complete!
hints: Put all 3 droid instances in a list
Workers call the Droid version of greet()
Commander calls the CommanderDroid version of greet()
This is polymorphism - same interface, different implementations!
